why_pinned: The sa1 base assembles this tree inside its own build (Config/SA1Pack.asm), and its Reproducible pin describes the cartridge that produces. That hash is only meaningful alongside the revision that produced it, so the two move together: changing this file is what makes a new sa1/U hash legitimate rather than a regression. The tree's clean-ROM guards read the initialize pass's empty image and so answer as on a clean cartridge, deterministically; the pin is what would move if a revision of the tree changed that.
why_this_revision: The working tree is 18 commits past the v1.40 tag and its changes.txt heads with 'SA-1 Pack v1.41', so v1.41 is in development and untagged upstream. The commit is therefore the identity and the ref is only a description of it. v1.41 is the revision that bumped the asar requirement to 1.90 and fixed I-RAM writes on boot that crashed accurate emulators -- which matters here, because Mesen is the core the editor embeds.
local_modifications: The first three make a block's applicability say what it means rather than borrow a proxy, and all inert on a clean ROM. (1) asm/sa1.asm: !remap_dp, !remap_addr, !remap_sram, !remap_map16 and !remap_dma switches around the five remap includes, all defaulting to 1. (2) asm/sa1.asm: the $00:8A60 bank-switch block probes its own output rather than a byte remap/addr.asm rewrites. (3) remap/sprite_memory.asm: gated on !remap_sprite_memory rather than that same borrowed byte -- %remap_memory is idempotent by construction, so the clean-ROM probe was belt-and-braces. Everything else is verbatim. Intended for upstream: any base that relocates work RAM in its own source reads as 'already patched' to the borrowed probe and silently loses these blocks. (4) remap/map16.asm: the $05D89C rewrite stands down under Define_SMW_TranslevelRemap -- which the assemble carries on its command line with the rest of the build's defines -- because that feature's JML occupies the read this patches and its own lookup already reads $40D000. Inert on a stock build. The overworld boost's literal seam at $048575 is instead honoured from the source side: the relocation feature pins an RTL at that address (Banks/Bank04.asm), so the boost runs unmodified over relocated builds. (5) remap/sprite_memory.asm: the bank each sprite list's header is patched in is read off the per-level table the managed level banks keep at the fixed tail of bank $07 ($07FE00) under Define_SMW_ManagedLevelMemory, because that feature packs sprite lists into whichever bank has room and the loader reads the same table; the stock $07 literal stands otherwise. Inert on a stock build. (6) more_sprites/more_sprites.asm: the pointer-indirect table dp_nontrivial_remap.asm is switchable (more_sprites_dp_nontrivial), because the sa1 base spells those accesses through its memory map's access defines and switches the table off; defaulting to 1, so an unmodified run is what it was. (7) more_sprites/more_sprites.asm: the two move tables and inc_max_sprites.asm are switchable together (more_sprites_moves), because the sa1 base places every sprite table and the slot count from its memory map; defaulting to 1. (8) asm/sa1.asm: the `asar 1.90` directive moved into asm/asar_version.asm and included unless sa1_code_in_pass is defined, because the directive sets asar's math mode -- C precedence and floating-point division -- for the whole assembly it appears in, bytes emitted before it included; a build that assembles this tree inside its own main pass (Config/SA1Pack.asm) keeps the mode its own sources were written for, and a run of the pack on its own reads the directive exactly as before. (9) asm/sa1.asm: the Super MMC bank-switch values take the pair asm/6mb.asm and asm/8mb.asm would write over them ($04-$07) when the including build defines sa1_rom_past_4mb, so a cartridge past 4 MB assembles in one pass; the two size files themselves are not run by this repository any more. (10) more_sprites/sprite_tables.asm: the define_sprite_table macro is left out when the including build defines sa1_sprite_table_macro_external, because asar allows one macro per name and a build that assembles this tree in-pass alongside UberASM Tool's macro library (which defines the same name with one column fewer) carries one macro that takes both spellings; an unmodified run defines it exactly as before.
why_modifiable: The Reproducible pin is what makes editing this tree safe: sa1/U must still assemble to produces_sha1, which was itself verified byte-identical to the patch applied to a real cartridge dump. An edit that changes behaviour changes that hash, and the gate fails.
migrated_to_source: remap/dp.asm, remap/addr.asm, remap/sram.asm, remap/map16.asm, remap/dma.asm and remap/sprite_memory.asm. The work-RAM remap is placed by smw/src's own memory map through !Define_SMW_DirectPageLocation and !Define_SMW_LowRAMLocation; the Map16 tables through !Define_SMW_Map16Location, the save files through !Define_SMW_SaveDataLocation, the DMA channels through !Define_SMW_OAMUploadDMAChannel, !Define_SMW_TilemapUploadDMAChannel and !Define_SMW_WindowHDMAChannel, and every eligible level's sprite memory index through !Define_SMW_SpriteMemoryIndex (Config/SpriteMemoryIndex.asm, a walk of the pointer tables on the finalize pass with the pack's own exclusions) -- every reader names the symbol, so one define moves them all, and the patch's copies are switched off with !remap_x=0. The result is byte-identical to the pack's own: sa1/U's hash did not move. Each pair has to move together: a source rebase changes bytes those blocks' own guards probe, so leaving one on would have it skip half its work and report nothing. One site is a port rather than a move: $00:9DBF's ADC.w #$01AD is the backup file's offset, which the source spells as the difference of two SRAM symbols so it stays an offset when the base moves the files. more_sprites/dp_nontrivial_remap.asm is expressed by the memory map's access defines: !RAM_SMW_NorSpr_XPosLo_x and its siblings expand to the shipped table on vanilla and to the pack's pointer on this base, held against the pack's own table by smw/tests/test_sa1_sprite_access.py, and the file is switched off. more_sprites/non_dp_remap.asm, dp_trivial_remap.asm and inc_max_sprites.asm: the memory map's SA-1 layout block (Memory/WRAM_DirectPage.asm) sets every sprite-table anchor to the pack's address and Define_SMW_MaxNormalSpriteSlot=$15 widens the loop bounds; the sites the pack leaves at a particular slot name !Define_SMW_StockMaxNormalSpriteSlot, sprite memory setting $08's last slot is its own define, and the seven direct-slot stores in code the pack replaces with its own (the two slot-8 spawns it JMLs over, the level-load init) name the _AsShipped tables, dead on this base. The pack's code -- engine, boosts, sa1.asm's vectors and trampolines, More Sprites' code and NMSTL -- and its one remaining table are assembled inside the main pass from the end of the ROM map (Config/SA1Pack.asm, `incsrc asm/sa1.asm` with the migrated parts switched off); its freespace search lands in bank $10 exactly as the retired patch pass's did. Byte-identical: the hash did not move.

differs_from_cartridge_by.summary: Seven bytes, plus the checksum pair that follows from them. Everything else is byte-identical to SA-1 Pack applied to a real USA cartridge dump, which is how this pin was first established and remains the check worth making after any upgrade. Four are the misdisassembled scrolling routines below; one more is in the same routine; two are the pack's own ordering quirk at $03:DEE3.

bytes.$05C666: cart $74, ours $14 -- the direct-page operand of `LDA.b $14`. With D=$3000 a direct-page access already reads $3014 and must not move; the patch relocates it to read $3074.
bytes.$05C672: cart $14, ours $74 -- the high byte of `STA.w $1464`, which the patch misses.
bytes.$05C6A8: cart $14, ours $74 -- the high byte of `LDX.w $1440`, which the patch misses.
bytes.$05C6AD: cart $14, ours $74 -- the high byte of `LDA.w $1446`, which the patch misses.
bytes.$05C6A4: cart $D8, ours $C2 -- the opcode of `REP #$20` in SMW_Layer1SpecialScrolling05_Unused, which the patch's remap tool read as the operand of an `LSR $C2,x` and rewrote to the state table's new offset. Same misdisassembly as the four above; nothing executes it.
bytes.$03DEE3-$03DEE4: cart $6E $32, ours $EA $EA -- two dead bytes after the `JML Mode7Stuff` the pack's boost/sprites.asm plants at $03:DEDF. The boost pads them with NOPs; the pack's non_dp_remap.asm, run afterwards in a single application, then writes `dw $326E` over them believing the original `LDA $14E0,x` is still there. That table is the memory map's now and no longer runs, so the NOPs stand -- which is also what a second application of the pack produces (docs/smw/sa1/patch-anatomy.md, Guards).

differs_from_cartridge_by.why_ours: All four are in SMW_Layer1SpecialScrolling05_Unused and SMW_Layer2SpecialScrolling06_Unused, which nothing calls. A community disassembly log renders both routines wrongly and the patch's remap tool inherits the error; this repository's reading was traced against the cartridge's bytes instruction by instruction. Nothing executes either way, so this is a correctness difference rather than a behavioural one -- but the pin should describe the more correct ROM.
